scenario: An ext4 mount at /srv/data carries the usrquota quota option in its super options; the requested path /srv/data/projects/app resolves to that ext4 mount, the mount major:minor equals the path st_dev, so the device check matches and the ext quota-option row classifies the path as enabled with unknown enforcement.

25 0 8:1 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/nvme0n1p2 rw,errors=remount-ro
26 25 0:21 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:11 - proc proc rw
27 25 0:22 / /sys rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:7 - sysfs sysfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec

30 25 0:41 / /srv rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:9 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=163840k,inode64

rationale: Contract section C2 mount resolution: mountinfo is parsed per proc.rst section 3.5 (S082, Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst:1965-1990), i.e. fields 1-6 are mount ID, parent ID, major:minor, root, mount point and per-mount options, optional 'tag[:value]' fields follow until the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and super options. Candidate mounts for realpath /srv/data are those whose mount point equals the realpath, is '/', or is a prefix at a '/' boundary: '/' (the ext4 root at 8:1), '/srv' (tmpfs at 0:41) and '/srv/data' (ext4 at 8:2). The longest mount point wins, so '/srv/data' (9 characters) is chosen over '/srv' (4) and '/' (1); the same mount covers realpath /srv/data/projects/app by the prefix rule, and both paths therefore report mount_point '/srv/data'. Contract section C2 device rule: the chosen fstype is ext4 (not btrfs) and its major:minor 8:2 equals the path st_dev 8:2, so the device check matches and classification proceeds. Contract section C2 quota-classification table, row 'ext2/ext3/ext4 | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota,prjquota,usrjquota,grpjquota | enabled | unknown | ext_quota_option': the super options of the chosen line are the last mountinfo field 'rw,usrquota', whose comma-split key 'usrquota' is one of the listed quota keys, so quota_state is enabled, enforcement is unknown (the ext quota feature state in the superblock is not observable from mountinfo alone, per the contract's stated limits), and the basis is ext_quota_option. The option name is the one documented for ext4 in Documentation/admin-guide/ext4.rst:261-265 (S083), which lists 'quota, noquota, grpquota, usrquota' as the ext quota mount options; the same document at :267-271 lists the journaled-quota forms usrjquota=<file> and grpjquota=<file>, which the contract's key-before-'=' rule reduces to the keys usrjquota and grpjquota. Contract section C2 verdict precedence: no setup error, and a path is enabled, so the run exits 1 with finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED (a runway-reporting finding, not a failure claim).
